mock_exam.weighting_note: 70% current module (21Q on M7 — all 6 items from levels 31-32 included in full, since those levels fall past the last checkpoint at level 30; 15 more spread across levels 1-30) / 20% same-phase review (6Q on M6, the oblique case) / 10% older high-value concepts (3Q on M4's gender-flagged words). This is the first mock to use the full three-way 70/20/10 split as specified, now that Module 7 has a genuine same-phase predecessor (M6) plus carried-forward concepts (gender) to draw on.
mock_exam.structural_note: Module 7 has 32 levels, not a multiple of 5, so its 6 checkpoints (after L5/10/15/20/25/30) leave levels 31-32 uncovered by any checkpoint. All 6 items from those levels are included in the mock.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The bare stem comes first and the marker second. Reversing them separates the verb from its own ending.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
options: मैं सो रहा था और फिर मैं सो रहा था
questions.explanation_en: A transitive perfective needs ने on the subject, and the participle then agrees with the object rather than with वह. Both halves of that arrive in Module 9.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The possessive needs the thing possessed behind it. Standing alone at the end of a phrase, की would be read as the verb instead.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The continuous describes one stretch of time in progress, which cannot be something that happens every day.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The habitual is a fact about his routine and says nothing about this moment, which is exactly what अभी is asking about.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: है ties the result to the present moment, which contradicts कल pointing back at yesterday.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: बैठो is the तुम form. Offering someone a seat in the wrong register undercuts the courtesy of offering at all.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: रहते belongs with तुम. When the speaker answers about himself the participle goes back to the singular रहता.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: Both words go plural. Leaving either one singular is the same half-correction this module keeps producing.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The future needs no auxiliary at all, and होगा is itself a future. Stacking them says nothing extra.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: हम is plural on both counts, so both the participle and the auxiliary have to be.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
options: मैं सो रहा था और फिर मैं सो रहा था
मैं सो रहा था और फिर मैं सोया
questions.explanation_en: The continuous describes an ongoing state and cannot narrate a completed event. Once something finishes, the aspect has to change.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The marker has to go plural too. Fixing only the auxiliary is the same half-correction that showed up in the habitual.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: जाया is what the rule predicts and it is not a word. जाना takes गया, and it is the only common verb that does anything this drastic.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The participle has to go plural too. Fixing only the auxiliary is the commonest half-correction at this level.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The marker agrees with the subject लड़की, which is feminine. किताब being feminine too is a coincidence here and not the reason.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: -एगा is singular. With no auxiliary present, the ending is the only thing marking the plural.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: -एंगे belongs to आप, हम and वे. Using it with तुम mixes two registers inside one sentence.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: होंगे belongs to आप, हम and वे. तुम has held plural agreement everywhere else in this module, so this is the one place it breaks step.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: जाएंगे is the future, which is a prediction rather than an instruction. मत only ever attaches to an imperative.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The participle comes first and the auxiliary sits behind it, exactly as with every other verb in the module.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: Two errors at once: भाई must shorten its vowel, and बहन has no vowel for a य to bridge.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The य and the shortened vowel belong to nouns ending in a long -ी. किताब ends in a consonant, so -ों attaches directly.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: में makes the possessed noun oblique, and the marker agrees with that noun in whatever state it is in.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: चाय is feminine, which is exactly why Module 4 asked you to memorise it. The masculine oblique -े never applies here.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: को governs both nouns, so बेटा must go oblique even though it is not the word sitting directly in front of the postposition.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: A postposition forces the oblique form, and बेटा changes to बेटे.

questions.prompt_en: Fill the blank: ___ परिवार ('family', my ...).
questions.explanation_en: परिवार ('family') is masculine.

questions.prompt_en: Fill the blank: ___ सिर ('head', my ...).
questions.explanation_en: सिर ('head') is masculine.

questions.prompt_en: Fill the blank: ___ पीठ ('back', my ...).
questions.explanation_en: पीठ ('back') is feminine.
